pairs.difference: A, the cooler, is one of the anchor's real cards. Its box turns from a lit left front to a darker right side, with soft contact darkening in the sand. On B, the pool rings are lit almost the same all the way round, with only a thin dark band under each tube. The fence also throws a hard, very dark diagonal shadow across the grass, which is harsher than the soft cast shadows on the real cards.
pairs.fix: Light the pool from the upper left so the right side of each ring falls into a soft mid-tone shadow. Give each tube a broad soft sheen on top. Make the fence shadow on the grass softer and lighter.

pairs.difference: A's envelope is lit flat from the front. The lens shows almost no change from left to right, the paper's shading keeps its own warm tint, and there is only a thin, faint shadow under the right edge. Its light bias (0.171) and shading range (0.631) both sit below the real cards. B's book has a clear lit top-left, a darker page block and spine, and a firm cast shadow to the lower right.
pairs.fix: Light the envelope from the upper left so its right and bottom edges fall into a clear soft shadow. Make the wax seal round with a bright spot on its upper left and a dark lower right. Add a soft cast shadow on the wood to the lower right.

pairs.difference: On A, the parasol's yellow canopy has one large glossy highlight. Under the pink ruffle the shading drops almost to black, so the light is pushed hard to one side (light bias 0.898 and shading range 0.835, both above the real cards). B's canopy panels each turn smoothly to a shaded underside, and its shadow depth matches the real cards.
pairs.fix: Lighten the inside of the parasol so the underside of the ruffle is a mid shadow, not black. Make the canopy highlight smaller and softer, and keep a gentle shadow side on the right.

pairs.difference: B's fan is lit almost flat. The pleats alternate light and dark as stripes, with no turn of form across each fold. The whole fan has no clear light or shadow side and only a faint cast shadow, and the lens keeps the fan's own purple tint. Form contrast (0.213) and light bias (0.09) are well below the real cards. A's gloves are rounded, with darker undersides at the fingers and cuffs and a soft cast shadow on the backdrop.
pairs.fix: Light the fan from the upper left. Shade each pleat so it turns from lit to shadow across its width, make the right half of the fan darker, and add a soft shadow under the fan.

pairs.difference: A's armchair is lit evenly from the front. The left and right arms are almost the same value, and the seat and back have little falloff (form contrast 0.325 and light bias 0.106, both below the real cards). B's rocking chair has lit tops on its rails, darker undersides and legs, and soft cast shadows of the rockers on the floor.
pairs.fix: Light the armchair from the upper left. Put the right arm and the right side panel in a clear shadow, darken the area under the seat cushion, and add a soft contact shadow under the legs.

pairs.difference: A's jacket looks soft like clay and is lit mostly from the front. Its body barely darkens toward the sides, and the green glow behind it tints the lens. B's top hat has a clear lit left crown, a smooth turn into a dark right side, and a glossy band. This is the real cards' side light.
pairs.fix: Light the jacket from the upper left. Give the right sleeve and right side of the body a clear soft shadow, and darken the inside of the collar and cuffs.

pairs.difference: A's inkwell is very dark on one side, and it throws a long, hard, near-black cast shadow to the right across the table. This is light pushed much harder to one side than on the real cards (light bias 1.192, form contrast 0.708). B's fountain has soft side shading on each basin and gentle shadows under the rims.
pairs.fix: Make the inkwell's cast shadow shorter, softer and lighter. Lift the shadow side of the glass jar with some soft bounce light from the table.

pairs.difference: A's ship wheel is lit straight from the front and is symmetrical. The rim and spokes are about the same value everywhere, with a washed-out, low-contrast lens (shading range 0.573, below the real cards). B's gramophone has a lit horn bell, a shaded inside, a darker box side and a clear contact shadow.
pairs.fix: Light the wheel from the upper left. Darken the lower right of the rim and the spoke handles, give the brass hub a small bright spot on its upper left, and add a soft shadow under the stand.

pairs.difference: A's spotlight has a neutral shading lens, a lit left barrel and a dark right side, and reads like the real cards' modeling. Its high light bias comes from the lamp being a light source. B's coral is lit from behind by a glowing yellow halo. The branches are lit about the same front to back, and the lens keeps the coral's warm color.
pairs.fix: Remove the glow behind the coral. Light it from the upper left so the right side of each branch darkens, and add soft contact shadows where the coral meets the rocks.

pairs.difference: B's pocket watch is lit flat from the front. The gold case has the same value all the way round, with no clear shadow side and only a faint sheen. A's ring box is lit from the top left, with a dark inner lid, a shaded right side and a crisp coin rim.
pairs.fix: Light the watch from the upper left. Darken the right and bottom of the gold case, put a small bright highlight on the upper left of the rim, and add a soft shadow under the case.

pairs.difference: A's door wall is covered in dappled leaf cast shadows, but the door and steps barely turn. The lens keeps the warm brick color, and light bias (0.186) is below the real cards. B's door has light from the left, shaded panel insets and a darker right frame.
pairs.fix: Light the door from the upper left. Shade the inside of each door panel and the right side of the frame and steps, and soften the leaf shadows on the wall.

pairs.difference: B's teacup has soft, low-contrast shading. The cup and saucer turn very gradually, and the lens has a dim falloff (shading range 0.584 and form contrast 0.36, both below the real cards). A's vending machine has a lit front, a clearly darker right side and crisp highlights on the glass and handle.
pairs.fix: Light the teacup from the upper left. Give the cup a clear dark right side, add a small bright highlight on the rim, and put a firm shadow of the cup on the saucer.

pattern: Generated cards often light the object evenly from the front. Left and right sides come out at the same value, forms barely turn into shadow, and the shading lens keeps the object's own color. The opposite failure is just as telling: light pushed too hard to one side, with near-black shadow sides, hard long cast shadows or glow halos. Real cards keep a steady top-left key, a smooth turn into a medium shadow on the right, and soft contact shadows.
